segments.headline: Laptop Wi-Fi keeps dropping?
segments.narration: Your laptop's Wi-Fi keeps dropping every few minutes, but every other device is fine? Here are 3 fixes, easiest first.

segments.headline: Windows puts your Wi-Fi card to sleep
segments.narration: Most of the time, Windows is putting your Wi-Fi card to sleep to save power, or it's running an old generic driver.

segments.headline: Turn off Wi-Fi power saving
segments.detail: Device Manager › Network adapters › Properties › Power Management
segments.narration: Open Device Manager, expand Network adapters, and open your Wi-Fi card's properties. On the Power Management tab, untick the box that lets Windows turn it off to save power.

segments.headline: Install the maker's newest driver
segments.detail: Intel, Realtek or your laptop's support page
segments.narration: Next, skip the driver Windows Update gave you. Download the newest one straight from Intel, Realtek, or your laptop maker's support page.

segments.headline: Reset your network settings
segments.detail: Settings › Network & internet › Advanced › Network reset
segments.narration: Still dropping? Open Settings, then Network and internet, then Advanced network settings, and hit Network reset. Heads up, it forgets your saved Wi-Fi passwords.

segments.headline: Don't use driver booster apps
segments.narration: And don't install driver booster apps. Many bundle junk and install the wrong driver.

segments.headline: Which fix worked for you?
segments.narration: Which one fixed yours? Tell me in the comments.

titles: Laptop Wi-Fi Keeps Disconnecting? 3 Fixes for Windows 11
Wi-Fi Drops Every Few Minutes on Windows 11? Try This
Fix Random Wi-Fi Disconnects on Your Laptop
upload.description:
Laptop Wi-Fi dropping every few minutes while other devices work fine?
1. Turn off Wi-Fi power saving in Device Manager
2. Install the newest driver from Intel, Realtek or your laptop maker
3. Use Network reset (it forgets saved Wi-Fi passwords)
Fixes collected from a r/techsupport discussion.
